set.body:
Objective:
Build optional ecosystem leverage around the completed Frame foundation without moving backend, format, numerical, or scheduler concerns into the pure core or turning the reference interpreter into a production engine.

Tracks:
- Parquet source/sink with truthful decode and pushdown capabilities.
- DuckDB engine with complete-plan translation first and Arrow batch handoff.
- A gated Polars/scala-polars collaboration or adapter spike that evaluates API stability, released artifacts, JVM/JNI lifecycle, typed coverage, semantic conformance, and Arrow handoff before any dependency is admitted.
- Gale numerical bridge with explicit null, chunk, layout, ownership, and allocation policies.
- Later evidence-driven spill, segmented execution, asynchronous pulls, and physical planning.
- Conformance, explain receipts, examples, and release boundaries for every optional artifact.

Architectural law:
Optional adapters depend on Frame. Frame does not depend on their implementations or semantics. The small JVM/Scala.js interpreter remains the semantic reference. Installing or omitting an adapter cannot change a Frame plan, schema, nullability, or default result contract. Production backends own physical optimization only within declared capabilities and must return residual work explicitly.

Incubation and publication:
Adapter artifacts use ScalaFIM naming while hosted here. If Frame is extracted and renamed, adapters migrate deliberately and independently. A Typelevel-candidate posture does not require every adapter to be cross-platform or to move into the same organization.

Out of scope unless a named consumer and conformance plan exist:
Spark translation, formula languages, regression/PCA APIs in Frame core, distributed schedulers, remote object stores, and universal zero-copy claims.

Epic acceptance:
Each admitted artifact has an explicit support matrix and independent lifecycle; at least one production backend demonstrates the value of the common plan without becoming a core dependency; unsupported translations fail structurally or leave visible residual plans; and Frame remains fully useful and testable with every optional adapter absent.
